_comment: Fleet session-worktree GC (scripts/worktree_gc.py). armed:false = report-only; deletion refuses. Flipping armed to true is the operator's ratification act — see research/WORKTREE_GC_POLICY.md before arming. JSON (not yml) so the tool runs on a bare system python3 under launchd with no pyyaml. The in-repo `.codex/worktrees` and the home-dir `~/.codex/worktrees` are DIFFERENT roots, not a duplicate — the in-repo one (55 checkouts) was missing until 2026-08-11. Registered worktrees are CLASSIFIED from `git worktree list` regardless of this list, so the miss was invisible in the report; what a missing root actually breaks is deletion (the final belt refuses any target `outside configured roots`, so a SAFE verdict there can never be acted on) and `scan_orphans`, which only walks configured in-repo roots. The in-repo roots must stay in step with `.gitignore`, `ship_loop_guard.AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOTS` and `worktree_create_sparse.SESSION_WORKTREE_ROOTS`; `tests/test_agent_worktree_roots.py` pins them. A RELATIVE root expands under EVERY host checkout of the clone (2026-08-20), not just the primary: this clone has two checkouts and session worktrees are planted beside whichever one the session was launched in, so expanding under the primary alone left the trees beside the other checkout out of `in_scope`, out of the report, and refused at the deletion belt.
_armed_ratification: OPERATOR RATIFIED 2026-08-13 (~02:45Z chat order: 'ok yes' to 'Arm the worktree GC — flip armed:true, optionally min_age_days 7->3'), during the disk-pressure incident: 1.7Ti/1.8Ti used, ~100GB free, two receipted runner ENOSPC crashes (2026-07-26, 2026-08-09), 168 session trees holding 386GB. min_age dropped 7->3 in the same act — at 7d the fleet's churn meant the gate never opened (150/168 trees read <7d on strong signals; 19 trees / 66GB age past 3d). Disarming again is likewise an operator act.
_human_driven_roots_comment: PURELY PROTECTIVE — adds refusals only; it can never cause a deletion, arm anything, or widen `roots`. Subtrees whose checkouts are driven by a HUMAN, honoured AHEAD of every verdict (worktree_gc.classify) and again at the deletion belt (apply_deletions), so removing one gate leaves the other. A Claude/Codex session is a shell and its silence is readable as death; a ChatGPT-web conversation has no shell or process and resumes the moment its human replies, so its attachment to a checkout is UNDETECTABLE and a valid landed proof is NOT permission — reclaim needs landed AND nothing attached, and the second half is unanswerable for this population. Measured 2026-09-26: an 'idle >= 24h' sparse sweep stripped 59 trees, 34 of them sol-*/review-* web trees, and essentially every ChatGPT session died unrecoverably. Before this key existed, 527 human-driven SSD checkouts were protected by exactly two ACCIDENTS — the narrow `roots` list and a host-checkout belt that classifies every absolutely-named tree as a host checkout — and the repair that makes a wider `roots` list delete anything removes both at once. NOT covered, stated rather than implied: loose `*-sol` trees directly under agent-workspaces are name-patterned, not a subtree, so this list cannot reach them; and agent-workspaces itself is deliberately NOT denied, because `.../agent-workspaces/claude` and `.../tmp` are the two subtrees that are safe to sweep.
